---
title: "Run the code"
description: >-
  What to install to run a lesson's experiment, to replay an agent lesson, or
  to check a proof, and what to do when a step fails.
---

Every figure and every number of a lesson comes from code in the
repository. Each lesson has an **experiment**: a program that computes what
the page shows and writes its figures and numbers into a folder of your
choice, so that you can change the code and run it again. The last section
of every lesson gives its commands. This page says what to install for each
of three things you may want to do:

1. **Run an experiment** of a simulation or a measured-data lesson. This
   needs Git and uv, and nothing else.
2. **Replay an agent lesson.** The same setup: the replay runs every tool
   call of a recorded run again, without a model and without a key. A live
   run with a model is a separate, optional step with your own account.
3. **Check a proof** of a Lean lesson, or work on its exercises. This adds the
   Lean toolchain.

None of these builds the website. Commands that the site's own checks run are
shown plainly. Every other command is marked "Not verified" and names the
account or key it needs.

## Run an experiment

A computer running macOS or Linux, about 1 GB of free disk space, and an
internet connection for the first run. Windows is not supported. Install
these two tools once; this is the only step that may need administrator
rights.

::: {.table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Tools to install"}

| Tool | Purpose | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Git | Source control | Xcode command line tools, or `brew install git` | System package manager |
| [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) | The pinned Python and the Python packages | `brew install uv` | `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh` |

:::

Then fetch the repository and its locked Python packages:

```{.bash .required-setup .python-only}
git clone https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction.git
cd physics-by-construction
uv sync --locked --no-dev
```

`--no-dev` installs the packages the lessons need, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib,
and PyYAML at the versions of `uv.lock`, and nothing else: no site generator,
no notebook kernel, no browser, and no test tools, which only the maintainers
of the site use.

Each lesson's experiment is a Python module of the repository. Its command,
from the folder of the clone, runs it and writes the figures of the page as
`<label>.png` and every number and table of the page, as the page shows
them, into `results/results.json`. For the first lesson:

```{.bash .experiment .simulation}
uv run --locked --no-dev python -m pbc.mechanics.experiments.kinematics results
```

A lesson that analyses measured data runs the same way; its data is a sample
committed to the repository:

```{.bash .experiment .measured-data}
uv run --locked --no-dev python -m pbc.mechanics.experiments.automated_analysis_pipelines results
```

The pattern, with the lesson's own module in place of the name in angle
brackets; the last section of every lesson names it:

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
uv run --locked --no-dev python -m pbc.<course>.experiments.<lesson> results
```
:::

The experiment of a lesson is in `src/pbc/<course>/experiments/`, and it calls
the lesson's code in `src/pbc/`. Change either and run the command again to
see what changes. The numbers match the page to the digits it shows; digits
beyond those can differ between machines, because floating-point libraries
differ.

## Replay an agent lesson

The agent lessons need no more than the setup above. Their experiment replays
the recorded run of the agent: it sends every tool call of the recording to
the allowlist and the simulation again, compares the results, and writes the
figures and numbers of the page. It calls no model and needs no key:

```{.bash .experiment .agent-replay}
uv run --locked --no-dev python -m pbc.mechanics.experiments.agent_experiment results
```

### Optional: a live run

This runs an agent lesson against a language model, with your own account.
It needs an OpenAI account and an API key, and the optional dependency
`openai`; it costs a few cents. The key stays in an environment variable of
your shell, never in a file or in code. The site never does this, so the
commands are not verified. The last section of each agent lesson names its
own module.

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
# needs: an OpenAI account and its API key, and the optional dependency openai
uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY="..."   # this shell only
uv run --locked --no-dev --extra openai python -m pbc.agents.projectile_lab
```
:::

## Optional: check a proof

The Lean lessons state theorems that a computer has checked. To check them
yourself, or to work on the exercises of
[Lean exercises on your machine](lessons/lean/04-lean-exercises-on-your-machine/index.qmd),
add the Lean toolchain. It needs no account, but about 11 GB of free disk
space for the Mathlib build cache.

::: {.table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="The Lean toolchain"}

| Tool | Purpose | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| [elan](https://lean-lang.org/install/manual/) | The pinned Lean toolchain | `brew install elan-init` | `curl -sSf https://elan.lean-lang.org/elan-init.sh \| sh` |

:::

Put `~/.elan/bin` on your `PATH`; the elan installer offers to do it. Then,
in the clone:

```{.bash .lean}
cd lean
lake exe cache get
lake build
```

`lake exe cache get` fetches the Mathlib build cache (about 0.5 GB, unpacking
to roughly 11 GB); never compile Mathlib yourself. `lake build` checks every
proof of the site; the last section of a Lean lesson names the modules of
that lesson. To work on an exercise, open the `lean/` folder in an editor
with Lean support, such as Visual Studio Code with the Lean 4 extension,
replace a `sorry`, and check the file:

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
# in lean/, after editing the exercise
lake env lean Exercises/ConstantAcceleration.lean
```
:::

## Optional: drive a coding agent

You can ask a coding agent, such as Claude Code or Codex, to write a
simulation from a specification. You choose the agent and supply its account
and credential; the site names none as a requirement and never runs one. The
rules of the sandbox profile (ADR 010) apply:

- Work in a scratch checkout, never in a checkout you care about.
- Let the agent run only the listed commands: the experiments, the tests, the
  formatter, and the lesson's own scripts.
- Give it no network access beyond its own provider. Its credential stays in
  your environment, in the variable that agent documents.
- Set a budget in steps, time, and cost before you start.
- Read every diff before you run it.

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
# needs: an account with the coding agent's provider, and its credential in
# your environment (see the agent's own documentation)
git clone https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction.git scratch
cd scratch
uv sync --locked --no-dev
# start your coding agent here, with the allowlist and budget set above
```
:::

## Troubleshooting

::: {.table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="What can go wrong and how to fix it"}

| What you see | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `git: command not found` or `uv: command not found` | A tool of the setup is missing | Install it from the first table |
| `uv sync --locked` says the lock file needs an update | `uv.lock` and `pyproject.toml` differ in your checkout | Check out a clean commit; do not run `uv lock` to get past it |
| `No module named 'pbc'` or `No module named 'pbc.mechanics.experiments'` | The command ran outside the folder of the clone, or before `uv sync` | Change to the folder of the clone and run `uv sync --locked --no-dev` first |
| An experiment stops with `ReplayMismatch` | The code of an agent lesson changed, so a recorded result no longer comes out | Expected after you change the code: the replay says which call differs. A live run records a new run |
| `No module named 'openai'` in a live run | The optional dependency is missing | `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra openai`, and run with `--extra openai` |
| The live agent says the key variable is not set | `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not exported in this shell | Export it in the shell that runs the command |
| `lake: command not found` | elan is missing, or `~/.elan/bin` is not on `PATH` | Install elan, then add `~/.elan/bin` to `PATH` and open a new shell |
| `lake exe cache get` cannot reach its host | The Lean release host or the cache host is unreachable from your network | Retry later or from another network |
| `lake` stops at a prompt for GitHub credentials while cloning Mathlib | GitHub refused an anonymous clone | Retry; if it persists, set a GitHub credential helper or run `gh auth login` |
| `lake build` starts to compile Mathlib | The build cache was not fetched or is incomplete | Stop it and run `lake exe cache get` again |

:::
